person_note: The controlling narration is close third person centered on Marina Singh. Goodreads provides several diagnostic passages that name or refer to Marina externally while rendering her background, perception, and learned knowledge, and authorized excerpts independently show the same structure in Chapter One and an interior Amazon scene. A whole-book POV guide explicitly calls the novel limited third person, and a contemporary review independently refers to its third-person narrator. First-person and second-person forms in the quote set belong to dialogue, generic maxims, or reported language; the authorized opening likewise embeds Dr. Swenson's first-person letter inside an otherwise third-person scene. No credible evidence of sustained narration in another person was found. The main limitation is that many popularity-selected quotes are aphorisms or dialogue, but the diagnostic quotes and separated authorized excerpts strongly agree.
